correctness.rationale: The 8 explicit cospherical vertices have 16 equal-length edges and supporting triangular and square faces; the normal chamber argument enumerates all signs by exact arithmetic in Q(sqrt2). The 56 triple determinants are nonzero, so the 58 constructed regions saturate Euler’s 58-cell bound; exact crossing counts are 24 of six and 34 of eight. Spherical opposite-sign probability of any equal-angle edge is arccos((2sqrt2−1)/7)/pi, yielding the stated distribution uniquely. The standalone checker reproduces the exact computation; an independent Gaussian-normal simulation corroborates the numerical probability.
